name: initialize_object_state
description: Stores its second argument as a longword in the object at offset 14, sets a 16-bit field at offset 18 to 40, stores the address of a global variable into a pointer field, and clears two longword fields. It only initialises those object fields.

name: delay_then_open_libraries
description: Busy-waits through a fixed count, then makes a series of library and dos calls that open resources and build their arguments on the stack. name: initialize_resource_entry

It writes a fixed four-byte marker into the new entry, then either builds a descriptor from entries at fixed offsets or forwards its arguments to another routine when the flag argument is non-zero, and finally stores the descriptor pointers in globals.

name: open_dos_or_build_list

Otherwise it compares a stored name with a string and, on a match, counts the nodes of a linked list and builds an array of pointer pairs from them.

name: stub_no_decompiled_body

name: copy_memory_block

name: split_command_line_into_tokens

name: append_string_to_destination

name: append_string_with_limit

name: run_setup_copy_and_init
description: Writes a parameter block and issues a device I/O call, then copies 768 bytes from a fixed source into low memory and fills seven longword slots with a constant. It clears all pending interrupt request bits, calls library functions, and when a flag argument is non-negative it allocates a structure and makes a few more calls before returning zero.

name: acknowledge_enabled_pending_interrupts
description: When the master-enable bit of the interrupt enable register is set, it writes back the pending requests that are also enabled, masked to the low fourteen bits, to acknowledge them. The routine returns its input value unchanged.

name: poll_port_bit_status
description: Computes a one-bit mask from a field of the structure, optionally sets an extra bit, and writes the inverted value to a CIA port register. It then polls a status bit of a global for a bounded count and returns when it clears; if it never clears, the decompiler shows a bad-instruction trap, which is not a real behaviour.

name: pulse_control_port_bits
description: Writes six fixed byte values to one control register at a fixed offset from the base register, clearing one bit at a time and restoring all bits at the start and end. It takes no data input.

name: wait_status_bit_then_clear
description: Loops while a status bit at a fixed offset from the base register is set, calling a routine on each pass. When the bit clears it zeroes a 16-bit field of the structure and returns.

name: step_position_with_pulses
description: Compares a requested position with the stored position in the structure, and when they differ it updates the stored value and pulses a control byte as many times as the difference, choosing the bit pattern by direction. Each pulse is followed by a fixed delay loop.

name: pulse_control_port_count
description: Pulses a control byte for a count held in a data register, writing two bit patterns on each pass with a fixed delay loop between writes. The base byte comes from a field of the structure.

name: read_value_with_retry_counter
description: Stores two arguments in the structure, then loops over a count, calling routines to read a value and decrementing a retry counter kept in the structure. When the counter expires it sets a flag byte, and it calls further routines before returning.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The decompiled body is only a bad-instruction trap, so the recovered code shows no usable behaviour. The facts list an exec forbid call, a device I/O library call and writes to the DMA and interrupt enable registers, but the body itself cannot be decoded.

name: unpack_bitstream_then_run_rle
description: Copies a fixed block of data into place and runs a bit-driven decoder that fills a buffer with literal and back-referenced bytes. It then expands escape-coded runs up to a fixed end address, and afterwards opens a library, runs unnamed routines inside a forbid-permit window, and closes the library.

name: refill_bit_buffer_word
description: Reads a longword just before the input pointer and writes its low byte, combined with the high byte of a register, as a 16-bit word through the output pointer. It returns that longword shifted right by one with the top bit set, which refills a bit buffer.

name: skip_bits_from_buffer
description: Shifts a bit buffer register right once for each of a count of bits passed in a data register, refilling the buffer from the stream when it empties. It makes no other changes and returns nothing.

name: open_graphics_library_then_close
description: Opens the library named by a global text pointer, which the referenced text gives as graphics.library, then calls three unnamed routines while multitasking is forbidden. It permits multitasking again, closes the library and returns zero.

name: step_value_until_flag
description: Loops until a flag is set and, on each pass, steps a 16-bit value by 273 between fixed limits, reversing direction at each limit. It returns once a completion flag is found set.

name: step_value_until_flag
description: The decompiled output for this entry matches its neighbour, so it shows the same loop: a flag wait that steps a 16-bit value by 273 between fixed limits and reverses at each limit. The facts list additional small constant-merge routines that the body does not show.

name: poll_beam_position_and_step
description: The facts show reads of the button port register and the vertical beam position counter, plus several small routines that merge constants into a data register. The decompiled loop is the same flag-wait and step body as its neighbours, so the beam-position link is taken from the facts.

name: draw_pattern_rows_and_advance
description: Advances a row counter and, when it reaches a fixed value, resets the counters and sets a flag. Otherwise it writes an eight-row pattern from a table into a bitplane at a position computed from two counters, with a stride of forty bytes between rows and a fill byte after each row.

name: clear_seven_rows_in_plane
description: Writes zero to one byte in each of seven rows of a bitplane, at a position computed from two counters, with a stride of forty bytes between rows. It returns nothing.

name: flag_line_end_characters
description: Reads one character through the address register, treating a zero byte as a full stop, and sets a global flag to one when the character is a line feed or tab. Otherwise it leaves the flag unchanged.

name: clear_fixed_memory_block
description: Writes zero to 16384 consecutive longwords starting at a fixed address, clearing 64 kilobytes of memory, then returns.

name: fill_tables_with_swapped_words
description: Loops for a count held in a data register, writing a halfword-swapped sum of three base values and a source word into three tables on each pass. It then steps each base value by a fixed amount, and one base value is reset to a fixed constant when it reaches a limit.

name: store_longword_halves_in_fields
description: Splits a longword argument into its high and low 16-bit halves and stores them in two 16-bit fields of the structure, at offsets two and six.

name: rotate_plane_columns_up
description: Decrements bytes in three columns of a bitplane at fixed steps, then rotates the bytes of each column one row upward, repeating the rotation for further columns according to a count. It works only on the bitplane data it is given.

name: step_values_up_every_fifteen
description: Counts ticks in a global and, every fifteen ticks, steps three 16-bit values up by 273 each time they differ from their targets.

name: step_values_down_on_tick
description: Counts ticks in a global, setting a completion flag when the count reaches 195. Every fifteen ticks it steps three 16-bit values down by 273 each time they differ from their targets.

name: advance_counter_until_small
description: Repeatedly adds a global value to a counter until the low nine bits of the sum drop to 255 or less. The facts list the beam position register, but the body shows only this counter loop.

name: select_row_offsets_from_table
description: Checks an index against a bound and traps when it is out of range, then fills three words before the address register with a fixed value. It reads table entries until one is not the terminator value, wrapping the table index at the terminator, and stores the entry times forty plus fixed offsets into two globals.

name: select_row_offsets_from_table
description: Same table walk as its neighbour without the bounds check: it fills three words before the address register with a fixed value, then picks a table entry and stores the entry times forty and an offset into two globals.

name: fill_word_select_row_offset
description: Fills one word before the address register with a fixed value, then reads table entries until one is not the terminator, wrapping at the terminator. It stores the entry times forty and an offset into two globals.

name: select_row_offset_from_table
description: Reads table entries until one is not the terminator value, wrapping the table index at the terminator. It stores the entry times forty and an offset into two globals.

name: read_swap_words_then_jump
description: Issues two device read requests, the first into a fixed buffer and the second into another, then swaps the 16-bit halves of each longword in a memory range before jumping into the loaded code at a fixed address. It then waits in an empty loop on a global value.

name: read_swap_and_jump_entry
description: Issues two device read requests, one into a buffer passed on the stack, then swaps the halves of 256 longwords in that buffer and jumps through the address stored at the buffer's fourth longword.

name: depack_stream_then_run_loop
description: Decodes a bit-packed stream with a bit reader that refills from the packed data, writing literal and back-referenced bytes backwards into a buffer. When the stream ends it calls a routine through a global table, sets output state, and runs a loop that waits for a timing flag and writes a colour register on each pass until a flag clears.

name: run_timed_frame_loop
description: Opens the graphics library through the exec base, sets a copper list pointer and DMA and interrupt enable writes, then runs a loop that waits on a flag, updates timing counters and calls routines until a status bit clears. It restores a saved value and returns.

name: clear_two_memory_ranges
description: Writes zero to every longword in two fixed address ranges, one range following the other at a fixed boundary.

name: copy_rows_while_waiting_status
description: Runs nested loops, waiting for a status value on each pass and calling routines while it counts passes. After each row it copies a block of words from a global buffer into a fixed destination with a stride of eight bytes.

name: copy_table_until_terminator
description: Copies longwords from a global table to a fixed destination address, one at a time, stopping after it copies the terminator value of minus two.

name: toggle_buffer_pair_and_flag
description: Tests a bit in a global and stores one of two fixed buffer addresses in each of two globals, in an order that depends on that bit, then sets or clears the bit. The two buffer addresses are fixed values 30720 bytes apart.

name: run_blitter_row_sequence
description: Writes blitter control words, then loops twenty times over four blitter register writes while advancing an offset that wraps when it passes 719. It then starts three more blitter operations, waiting for the blitter through a wait routine between them.

name: compute_scaled_offset_from_word
description: Reads a 16-bit value through the address register, subtracts seventy-five, and returns the result multiplied by fifty.

name: set_blitter_pointers_and_start
description: Writes a control value and three pointer values into blitter registers, each pointer offset from the address arguments by a fixed amount. It then writes a size word that starts the operation and returns two.

name: map_character_to_table_value
description: Reads the next nonzero character from a string pointer. A digit one, an S, and any other character each pick a different table value, while full stops, exclamation marks and capital I share another, and the chosen value is stored in a global before a routine is called.

name: map_character_to_table_value
description: Sets bit one of a flag byte, then performs the same character mapping as its neighbour: it reads the next nonzero character and stores a table value chosen by that character in a global before calling a routine.

name: setup_blitter_row_pairs
description: Writes blitter control words and a fixed constant, then runs three passes that write two pointer values and a size word for blitter operations, stepping both pointers by a fixed plane offset on each pass.

name: copy_pairs_to_strided_buffer
description: Copies four pairs of longwords from a global buffer into a destination that advances ten longwords per pass, writing the two halves of each pair in sequence.

name: setup_blitter_two_rows
description: Writes blitter control values from globals, then runs two passes that write two pointer values and a fixed size word, stepping both pointers by a fixed plane offset on each pass.

name: call_routines_with_marker_writes
description: Calls a series of routines in pairs, writing the value fifteen into a global five times between the calls. It returns after the last call.

name: copy_sequence_repeatedly_until_terminator
description: Copies longword sequences from a source to a destination, each sequence ending at the terminator value of minus two, and repeats the whole copy for a fixed number of passes.

name: write_stepped_characters_into_buffer
description: Loops over a count, writing a running character value and a value copied from a source array into a buffer at a stride of 64 bytes. The character value increases by a step read from a global on each pass.

name: update_interleaved_plane_columns
description: Adds one to bytes in two interleaved columns at a stride of 64 bytes and adds two to a third column. Every second call it also adds one to a fourth column, then toggles bit zero of a fifth column, all over a fixed count.

name: draw_text_glyphs_to_bitplane
description: Draws a block of text by walking a string row by row, copying each character's seven-row glyph from a font table into a destination with a stride of fifty bytes. It advances to the next row by a fixed offset after each row.

name: disable_audio_playback
description: Clears the audio playing flag and zeroes four audio channel period registers. It then writes a four-channel mask into a shadow of the audio DMA control word with one bit cleared.

name: initialise_audio_channel_records
description: Sets the audio playing flag, writes setup values to the DMA and interrupt registers, and reads a tempo byte from a song header, using three when that byte is zero. It builds channel records by clearing their fields and filling sample offsets, lengths and volumes from a source table, with running addresses computed for each record.

name: update_audio_channels_each_tick
description: When audio is playing it decrements a tick counter and, when the counter expires, reloads it and calls routines to advance each channel. It then writes each channel's location, length and period values into the audio registers and writes the DMA control word.

name: advance_audio_channel_stream
description: Advances one audio channel record through its song stream. When the step counter reaches its limit it fetches the next pattern entry, then sets the sample address, length and volume fields used by the audio update, and it sets the channel's DMA bit in a shared mask.

name: interpret_music_stream_commands
description: Walks a channel's music stream, handling command bytes that set an instrument, a note offset or a jump address, and copying note bytes into channel fields. When the note ends it computes a period clamped between fixed limits and returns it with a volume byte. The decompiled output is truncated, so this covers only the visible part.

name: set_control_byte_bits
description: Sets one bit in a control byte and writes a value into the byte before it. It then tests a condition that the decompiled expression cannot satisfy, so the remaining path ends in a bad-instruction trap, and only the byte writes are real behaviour.
